3D beam mechanics · Bending + torsion

FROM IMAGE TO MATERIAL

Branches within branches.

The reference is interpreted as a family of connected cellular networks, with thick load-bearing walls, finer internal branches, irregular pores, and repetition across scales.

This note is saved with the design. Geometry follows the numerical controls; the image is inspiration rather than a dimensioned reconstruction.
MECHANICS NOTEBOOK

A physical model you can inspect.

The 3D unit cell is a connected volume of struts. Each node has three translations and three rotations. Circular spatial beams carry axial force, bending moments in both transverse directions, and torque. Finite rotation vectors transport material directors; the energy is invariant to a common rigid translation and rotation.

A = πr² · I = πr⁴/4 · J = 2I
N = Aσ · torsional stiffness = GJ/L

3D cell families

Kelvin foam uses truncated-octahedron edges arranged on a body-centered cubic lattice. Organic disorder perturbs its nodes. Branching and nested cages create smaller internal length scales. Octet, diamond, and re-entrant cells provide alternative spatial architectures. X, Y, and Z repeats merge shared face nodes into one mechanical specimen. “Re-entrant” describes geometry; a negative measured Poisson ratio is not assumed.

Materials and equilibrium

Choose linear elasticity, Neo-Hookean axial elasticity, or axial elastoplasticity with isotropic hardening. Bending and torsion retain elastic reference sections. G = E/[2(1 + ν)]; the incompressible axial option uses G = E/3. The spatial solver differentiates its discrete energy by automatic differentiation and uses a sparse quasi-Newton solve with an energy line search. Animation shows quasi-static solver progress, not physical time.

Experiments

Select the loading axis. The lower face fixes all six degrees of freedom. Tension/compression prescribe the upper face’s axial displacement and rotations while allowing transverse translation. Shear prescribes one perpendicular translation and holds the face separation. The response chart records converged steps only. Maximum |ΔZ| and torsional energy expose spatial response.

Notch and fracture

The notch is a cut in a constant-Y plane, extending from the left X boundary. Its Z extent controls whether the crack front spans the depth or is a centered partial-depth slit. Every crossing parent strut is removed. Optional failure combines axial/bending normal stress and torsional shear into the maximum tensile principal stress at the beam surface. The worst over-strength strut is deleted, then equilibrium is resolved. This strength criterion is not a calibrated fracture-energy law.

Print geometry

STL export includes the full spatial network and all XYZ repeats. Profiles are circular struts, reinforced junctions, or square-section struts. The exporter samples the implicit union in slices. Raw budgets default to 8M triangles and 128M grid samples, with options up to 16M and 512M. Adaptive simplification reduces smooth regions using a surface-error target and curvature retention, with optional locked junctions/tips. The output is checked for closed edges, orientation, component count, Euler characteristic, and volume change. Grid size limits accuracy; thickening and cross-section changes occur after the mechanics solve. The cutaway is visual only and never changes mechanics or the STL.

Replay and experiment results

Runs are automatically saved under Results with their exact settings, measurements, failure events, and available replay geometry. Pause or finish an experiment to replay it and export an MP4. Smooth replay interpolates positions for display; it holds measured values from the preceding state and preserves discrete fracture. Video duration is presentation time, not physical time. Results provides comparison curves, summary scatter plots, CSV/SVG export, and full data ZIP import/export. Solver Reset keeps earlier experiments; Results → Reset results clears the collection. Data stays in this browser and origin; use a data ZIP to move it or preserve a backup.

Scope and compatibility

This is a reduced-order 3D beam model, not a solid-element continuum analysis. It captures out-of-plane deformation, bending, and torsion, but does not include self-contact, shear deformation, plastic hinges, solid-junction stress concentrations, print defects, or fracture toughness calibration. Large local beam rotations and thick/short struts can exceed its approximation. A local quasi-static solver can fail near an instability; the residual and convergence status remain visible. Version 1 designs reopen in planar mode, where the original 2D solver and fabrication-only layer option remain available.

Background: corotational frame transformations · spatial beam mechanics. Canopy’s director-energy solver is independently implemented.
